title: Choose a projection recovery path, then walk the cutover
description: Select an incident and a runbook. Advance each stage to see which state remains authoritative, what readers observe, and what evidence is required before a rebuilt read model can take traffic.

scenarios.label: A handler bug corrupted order totals
scenarios.detail: The event history is valid, but one deployed projector double-counted discounts in the current read model.
scenarios.symptom: Reconciliation finds order-summary totals that disagree with a fold over the authoritative order streams.

plans.label: Build a versioned projection beside the current one
plans.detail: Fix the handler, replay into a clean target, validate it, then switch the read alias.
plans.verdict: The corrupted model is replaced only after deterministic replay and business reconciliation prove the candidate.

stages.label: Contain
stages.action: Freeze projector v1, mark affected totals as degraded, and preserve its checkpoint and logs for diagnosis.
stages.result: The bad handler stops writing. Reads remain available but explicitly stale or degraded while the team prepares a clean target.

event-store.detail: Validated order events remain immutable and readable.

current-projection.detail: Known-wrong totals are quarantined from decisions that require correctness.

candidate-projection.detail: No candidate exists yet.

read-alias.detail: The UI serves degraded data or disables total-dependent actions.

stages.label: Replay
stages.action: Deploy fixed handler v2 into a new order-summary-v2 target and replay from the beginning with an independent checkpoint.
stages.result: The old projection is untouched. The candidate can restart from its own checkpoint without moving the production consumer position.

event-store.detail: Historical and newly appended events feed the isolated v2 projector.

current-projection.detail: The known-bad v1 target is preserved for comparison only.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 folds every event with the corrected discount rule.

read-alias.detail: Readers have not been switched to the incomplete candidate.

stages.label: Verify
stages.action: Catch up to the live stream, compare event positions, reconcile sampled aggregates, and verify duplicate-event behavior.
stages.result: Matching checkpoints prove only completeness. Domain reconciliation is still required to prove that the new fold is correct.

event-store.detail: The candidate checkpoint reaches the agreed high-water mark.

current-projection.detail: v1 remains the known-bad comparison baseline.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 is caught up and passes deterministic and business-level checks.

read-alias.detail: Traffic still waits for an explicit cutover decision.

stages.label: Cut over
stages.action: Atomically point the read alias to v2, monitor correctness and lag, then retain v1 for a bounded rollback window.
stages.result: Readers move as one controlled release. The event store remains the recovery source if the candidate later fails.

event-store.detail: Authoritative history is unchanged by the projection release.

current-projection.detail: v1 is read-only and scheduled for retirement after the rollback window.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 continues from its verified checkpoint.

read-alias.detail: Queries now resolve to the corrected v2 model.

verification: Candidate checkpoint equals the agreed event-store high-water mark and continues advancing.
Representative order totals match an independent fold of the same event streams.
Replayed duplicate event IDs do not change totals or repeat external side effects.
The alias switch and bounded rollback procedure have both been exercised.

plans.label: Truncate and rebuild the production table
plans.detail: Reuse the existing target and checkpoint after taking the read model offline.
plans.verdict: This can be valid only when the product accepts an outage or fully isolated maintenance window.

stages.label: Stop
stages.action: Stop production reads and the v1 projector before changing the shared table.
stages.result: A hard availability decision is now part of the recovery plan.

event-store.detail: Writes continue to append authoritative events.

current-projection.detail: The only read target is offline.

candidate-projection.detail: No isolated candidate is created.

read-alias.detail: Queries are unavailable or routed to a documented fallback.

stages.label: Clear
stages.action: Archive evidence, truncate the shared projection, reset only its checkpoint, and deploy the corrected handler.
stages.result: The bad rows are gone, but there is no complete read model until replay finishes.

event-store.detail: History remains the rebuild source.

current-projection.detail: The empty production target begins replay.

candidate-projection.detail: Isolation is intentionally not used.

read-alias.detail: Serving a partially rebuilt table would expose incomplete results.

stages.label: Verify
stages.action: Wait for catch-up, reconcile totals, and verify idempotency before restoring queries.
stages.result: The same correctness proof is required even though the target name did not change.

event-store.detail: The projector reaches the selected high-water mark.

current-projection.detail: The shared target is complete and verified.

candidate-projection.detail: There is no alternate target for side-by-side comparison.

read-alias.detail: Readers stay offline until validation completes.

stages.label: Resume
stages.action: Restore the read alias and monitor projection lag, correctness, and request errors.
stages.result: The model is repaired, but the recovery consumed the full read outage budget.

event-store.detail: Event appends continue normally.

current-projection.detail: The rebuilt table is live.

candidate-projection.detail: No parallel version exists.

read-alias.detail: Queries return only after the complete rebuild.

verification: The maintenance window explicitly covers the complete replay and verification period.
No reader can access a partially rebuilt target.
The rebuilt checkpoint and independent business reconciliation agree.
A restore or alternate read path exists if the in-place rebuild fails.

plans.label: Fix the handler and resume from its checkpoint
plans.detail: Continue processing new events without rebuilding rows already written by the buggy handler.
plans.verdict: New writes may be correct, but historical corruption remains in every affected row.

stages.label: Patch
stages.action: Deploy corrected code without changing the target or checkpoint.
stages.result: The handler bug is fixed only for events processed after the deployment.

event-store.detail: The authoritative events were never damaged.

current-projection.detail: Rows created by the old code retain incorrect totals.

candidate-projection.detail: No clean target is built.

read-alias.detail: Queries still expose historical corruption.

stages.label: Resume
stages.action: Restart from the existing checkpoint and process only later events.
stages.result: Checkpoint continuity proves processing progress, not correctness of the existing rows.

event-store.detail: New events continue after the saved position.

current-projection.detail: Correct new deltas are applied to an incorrect base.

candidate-projection.detail: There is still no clean comparison model.

read-alias.detail: Users see a mixture of old corruption and new correct handling.

stages.label: Observe
stages.action: Watch lag return to normal while reconciliation still reports wrong totals.
stages.result: A healthy lag metric can coexist with a semantically incorrect read model.

event-store.detail: The source remains complete.

current-projection.detail: The model is caught up but still wrong.

candidate-projection.detail: No repair path exists.

read-alias.detail: Request health hides data-quality failure.

stages.label: Escalate
stages.action: Stop treating checkpoint progress as recovery and start a clean rebuild or explicit correction.
stages.result: The original plan never repaired the corrupted historical state.

event-store.detail: History can still power the correct recovery.

current-projection.detail: The target remains unsuitable for trusted decisions.

candidate-projection.detail: A clean target must still be created.

read-alias.detail: Degraded behavior must continue until a real repair completes.

verification: Historical rows are regenerated or corrected, not merely followed by correct new rows.
Business reconciliation passes independently of checkpoint and lag metrics.
The corrected handler is proven deterministic across a full replay.

scenarios.label: Product needs a new read-model shape
scenarios.detail: A new order-search experience needs different fields and indexes, while the existing read API must remain available.
scenarios.symptom: The current model is correct, but its schema cannot answer the new query without expensive joins and application-side assembly.

plans.label: Create projection v2 and cut over by alias
plans.detail: Replay history into the new shape while v1 continues serving production.
plans.verdict: The new query model ships as an independently verified release without turning schema migration into an outage.

stages.label: Contract
stages.action: Define the v2 query contract, ownership, indexes, checkpoint, and acceptance samples before starting replay.
stages.result: The target has a measurable purpose rather than becoming another accidental copy of domain state.

event-store.detail: History contains the facts needed for both read shapes.

current-projection.detail: v1 continues serving its existing contract.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 schema and handler are prepared in isolation.

read-alias.detail: Existing queries still resolve to v1.

stages.label: Replay
stages.action: Build v2 from the event stream with its own checkpoint and catch up to live events.
stages.result: The candidate evolves without mutating v1 or resetting its consumer position.

event-store.detail: The same ordered history feeds v1 and v2 independently.

current-projection.detail: v1 processes live events as before.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 replays history and then follows the live tail.

read-alias.detail: Production remains on v1 during replay.

stages.label: Shadow
stages.action: Compare v1-compatible fields, verify new query results, and shadow representative requests against v2.
stages.result: Completeness, performance, and product semantics are tested before user traffic depends on v2.

event-store.detail: Both projectors share the same high-water mark.

current-projection.detail: v1 remains the production baseline.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 passes contract and reconciliation checks.

read-alias.detail: Shadow traffic does not affect user responses.

stages.label: Release
stages.action: Switch the query route to v2, observe the release, and retire v1 only after the rollback window.
stages.result: Projection versions become deployable artifacts with independent lifecycles.

event-store.detail: No event history is rewritten for the new view.

current-projection.detail: v1 remains available for bounded rollback.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 serves the new and preserved query contracts.

read-alias.detail: Production queries now route to v2.

verification: v2 exposes a documented query contract and owner.
Its checkpoint catches the agreed event-store high-water mark.
Comparable v1 and v2 fields reconcile for sampled aggregates.
The alias can switch back to v1 inside the rollback window.

plans.label: Alter v1 in place during live traffic
plans.detail: Change the serving schema and handler without an isolated target.
plans.verdict: This couples migration, replay, and serving into one failure boundary and needs a carefully bounded maintenance plan.

stages.label: Alter
stages.action: Apply schema changes to the live projection while existing readers still use it.
stages.result: Old and new application versions can observe a transitional schema.

event-store.detail: History is unaffected.

current-projection.detail: The live target is between contracts.

candidate-projection.detail: No isolated schema exists.

read-alias.detail: Readers must tolerate both shapes or stop.

stages.label: Backfill
stages.action: Populate new fields in the same table while live updates continue.
stages.result: Backfill and tail processing must coordinate without missing or overwriting changes.

event-store.detail: Events continue to arrive.

current-projection.detail: One target handles serving, backfill, and live updates.

candidate-projection.detail: There is no clean comparison target.

read-alias.detail: Some rows may not yet satisfy the new contract.

stages.label: Verify
stages.action: Prove every row has the new fields and old readers remain compatible.
stages.result: Correctness depends on migration choreography rather than a simple target swap.

event-store.detail: The source can still support a clean rebuild if needed.

current-projection.detail: The in-place model appears complete.

candidate-projection.detail: No independent baseline exists.

read-alias.detail: Cutover is inseparable from the schema state.

stages.label: Complete
stages.action: Remove compatibility code after all readers and rows use the new contract.
stages.result: The migration can work, but rollback after destructive changes is harder than switching aliases.

event-store.detail: History remains the final recovery source.

current-projection.detail: The original target now serves the new shape.

candidate-projection.detail: No versioned target was retained.

read-alias.detail: Queries use the migrated v1 target.

verification: Every reader supports the transitional and final schemas.
Backfill and live updates cannot overwrite each other.
Rollback is tested before destructive schema changes.
The maintenance and error budget includes the coupled migration risk.

plans.label: Query raw event streams from the product API
plans.detail: Skip a projection and replay many aggregates for every user query.
plans.verdict: The product query now pays replay cost and couples clients to historical event versions.

stages.label: Bypass
stages.action: Route search requests directly to event-stream reads.
stages.result: The event store is asked to serve a query model it was not designed to expose.

event-store.detail: Interactive queries scan and fold many event streams.

current-projection.detail: v1 remains available but cannot answer the new shape.

candidate-projection.detail: No purpose-built model is created.

read-alias.detail: User latency now depends on unbounded replay work.

stages.label: Expand
stages.action: Add handling for every historical event version inside the query path.
stages.result: Schema evolution logic and product serving are tightly coupled.

event-store.detail: Historical versions must remain interpretable.

current-projection.detail: Existing product queries still use v1.

candidate-projection.detail: There is still no indexed query shape.

read-alias.detail: Query correctness depends on inline upcasting and replay.

stages.label: Pressure
stages.action: Observe product traffic competing with command rehydration and projection subscriptions.
stages.result: One new read feature expands the blast radius of the authoritative store.

event-store.detail: Serving pressure threatens recovery and command workloads.

current-projection.detail: v1 is not the source of the new pressure.

candidate-projection.detail: No decoupled read capacity exists.

read-alias.detail: Latency and availability depend on event-store load.

stages.label: Replace
stages.action: Stop direct product queries and build the missing versioned projection.
stages.result: The original plan never established a stable read contract.

event-store.detail: The source returns to append, rehydration, and controlled replay duties.

current-projection.detail: v1 continues serving known queries.

candidate-projection.detail: v2 still needs to be designed and built.

read-alias.detail: The new feature waits for a real query model.

verification: Product queries use a bounded, owned read contract.
Historical event-version handling stays out of the request critical path.
The event store retains capacity for commands, recovery, and subscriptions.

scenarios.label: The projector was offline but its checkpoint is healthy
scenarios.detail: No handler bug occurred. The subscription stopped during a database outage, and the sink remains internally correct up to its saved checkpoint.
scenarios.symptom: Projection lag grows while event-store appends remain healthy; reconciliation is correct through the durable checkpoint.

plans.label: Resume from the durable checkpoint
plans.detail: Repair the sink, restart the idempotent handler, and consume forward from the saved position.
plans.verdict: The projection catches up without replaying already verified history or resetting its correctness boundary.

stages.label: Diagnose
stages.action: Confirm that the event store is healthy, the sink outage is repaired, and the saved checkpoint matches durable sink state.
stages.result: The incident is classified as missing later events, not corrupted earlier state.

event-store.detail: Events continue beyond the consumer checkpoint.

current-projection.detail: Rows are correct only through the saved position.

candidate-projection.detail: A clean rebuild is not yet justified.

read-alias.detail: The product exposes or tolerates bounded staleness.

stages.label: Resume
stages.action: Restart the same handler from its durable checkpoint with bounded concurrency and idempotent writes.
stages.result: Only events after the verified position are applied.

event-store.detail: The subscription reads from the saved position.

current-projection.detail: The sink catches up without clearing correct rows.

candidate-projection.detail: No parallel target is needed.

read-alias.detail: Readers remain behind while backlog drains.

stages.label: Catch up
stages.action: Watch oldest-unprocessed event age and checkpoint progress rather than only events per second.
stages.result: Falling event age proves the consumer is gaining on the live tail.

event-store.detail: Source append health remains stable.

current-projection.detail: Checkpoint and data rows advance together.

candidate-projection.detail: No duplicate rebuild workload is introduced.

read-alias.detail: Freshness improves as event age falls.

stages.label: Verify
stages.action: Reach the live high-water mark, reconcile representative rows, and close degraded product behavior.
stages.result: Progress and correctness evidence agree before the incident is closed.

event-store.detail: The source and consumer positions converge.

current-projection.detail: Rows are current and reconciliation passes.

candidate-projection.detail: No alternate target was required.

read-alias.detail: The product returns to its freshness objective.

verification: The saved checkpoint and durable sink writes share a defined atomicity or idempotency contract.
Oldest-unprocessed event age returns inside the freshness objective.
Representative read rows reconcile after catch-up.
Duplicate delivery around the restart does not change outcomes.

plans.label: Start a full shadow rebuild
plans.detail: Replay all history into a second target even though the existing target is correct through its checkpoint.
plans.verdict: The plan can recover, but it spends more source, sink, and operator capacity than the evidence requires.

stages.label: Allocate
stages.action: Create a second target and an independent subscription from the beginning.
stages.result: The incident now includes a full historical replay.

event-store.detail: Historical replay competes with live command reads and subscriptions.

current-projection.detail: Correct rows through the old checkpoint remain unused for recovery.

candidate-projection.detail: The candidate starts from zero.

read-alias.detail: Freshness waits for a much longer rebuild.

stages.label: Replay
stages.action: Process the entire history while live events continue to arrive.
stages.result: The candidate recomputes state that the current target had already proven.

event-store.detail: Replay load must be bounded to protect production.

current-projection.detail: The existing target stays behind.

candidate-projection.detail: The full rebuild advances toward the live tail.

read-alias.detail: Users still observe old data.

stages.label: Verify
stages.action: Reconcile the candidate even though no handler or historical-data bug was observed.
stages.result: The same correctness proof remains necessary before cutover.

event-store.detail: The candidate finally reaches the high-water mark.

current-projection.detail: The old target remains a comparison source.

candidate-projection.detail: The rebuilt target matches the correct existing data.

read-alias.detail: Cutover has not yet occurred.

stages.label: Cut over
stages.action: Switch to the candidate and retire the old checkpoint.
stages.result: Correctness returns, but recovery time and production load were unnecessarily high.

event-store.detail: Historical replay ends.

current-projection.detail: The old correct-through-checkpoint target is retired.

candidate-projection.detail: The rebuilt target becomes production.

read-alias.detail: Queries finally become current.

verification: Replay is rate-limited so it cannot damage event-store or sink SLOs.
The candidate is reconciled before cutover.
The longer recovery objective is explicitly accepted.
Operators document why a verified checkpoint was not reused.

plans.label: Reset the checkpoint but keep existing rows
plans.detail: Replay history into the populated sink without proving every write is idempotent.
plans.verdict: The plan can double-count historical events and turn a lag incident into data corruption.

stages.label: Reset
stages.action: Move the consumer position to the beginning while leaving current projection rows in place.
stages.result: Every historical event is now eligible for duplicate application.

event-store.detail: The source correctly re-delivers history.

current-projection.detail: Existing rows may receive every delta a second time.

candidate-projection.detail: No clean target isolates the replay.

read-alias.detail: Readers remain connected to the mutation target.

stages.label: Replay
stages.action: Process old events through handlers that were designed only for forward progress.
stages.result: Counters, notifications, and non-idempotent updates can repeat.

event-store.detail: Historical delivery behaves as requested.

current-projection.detail: Duplicate effects accumulate in the populated sink.

candidate-projection.detail: There is no clean baseline.

read-alias.detail: Users can observe drifting values during replay.

stages.label: Detect
stages.action: Reconciliation discovers values exceeding any state derivable from the source events.
stages.result: The recovery action created a second, more severe incident.

event-store.detail: Authoritative history still contains each fact once.

current-projection.detail: The sink contains duplicate derived effects.

candidate-projection.detail: No trustworthy candidate exists.

read-alias.detail: The projection must be withdrawn.

stages.label: Rebuild
stages.action: Stop the replay and rebuild into a clean target or restore a verified checkpoint.
stages.result: The checkpoint reset was not a valid substitute for idempotent processing.

event-store.detail: The source can still power a clean recovery.

current-projection.detail: The duplicate-mutated target is quarantined.

candidate-projection.detail: A real recovery target must still be created.

read-alias.detail: Queries remain unavailable or degraded.

verification: Projection writes are idempotent by stable event identity or deterministic replacement.
Checkpoint movement cannot expose a populated sink to unsafe duplicate deltas.
Reconciliation compares derived state with the authoritative event history.
